title: Equivariant extension of the contraction under (K3)
body_html:
Equivariant extension of the contraction under (K3)

Setting: fixed vertex $x \in A$; $c : C_d(A) \to C_{d+1}(A)$ from Contraction map c: C_d(A) → C_{d+1}(A) (Bestvina–Savin); hypothesis (K3) from [[node:building.K3_hypothesis]].

Lemma (Sheaf7 §5.2). Under (K3), the contraction map $c$ extends uniquely to a map $$c : C_d(\BSigma_x) \to C_{d+1}(\BSigma_x)$$ such that $$c(k \cdot E) = k \cdot c(E) \qquad \forall k \in \Fix_G(x),\ E \in [\![\BSigma_x]\!]_d,$$ and for every cell $E$ in $\BSigma_x$, $\partial c(E) + c(\partial E) = E$.
proof_html:
Well-definedness reduces to: if $kE = E$ then $c(E) = k \cdot c(E)$. The condition $kE = E$ implies $k \in \Fix_G(y)$ for every $y \in \overline E$. For each $E'$ with $c(E, E') \ne 0$, property (C2) of $c$ gives $y \in \overline E$ with $E' \cap [y, x] \ne \emptyset$. Pick $z \in E' \cap [y, x]$. By (K3): $$k \in \Fix_G(x) \cap \Fix_G(y) \;\subseteq\; \Fix_G(z) = \Fix_G(E'),$$ so $k \cdot E' = E'$ and $c$ is $k$-equivariant on $E$. The chain-homotopy identity follows from (C3) plus the cell-face inclusion lemma from §2.8. $\square$

This $\Fix_G(x)$-equivariant extension is what powers Acyclicity of C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x] for vertices x (acyclicity of $C_\bullet(\Phi, V)[\phi_x]$).
